chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about tayammum in place of wudu (ablution), and in place of janabah, and in place of menstruation for women—are they the same? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed as a substitute for water-based purification
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, a state involving rulings of ritual purity for women
key_terms.لِلنِّسَاءِ: for women, indicating the ruling’s application to female menstruation

ai.seo_question: Is tayammum the same for wudu (ablution), janabah, and menstruation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that tayammum applies equally as a substitute purification in cases of wudu (ablution), janabah, and menstruation for women. It presents a concise legal ruling concerning ritual purity and the uniformity of tayammum across these states.
